overall: No violation found by the School Committee; the complaint was resolved by informal action. Allegations of manipulation, secrecy, and employee conduct were declined, and the Student Nominations Committee was found not to be a public body.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged children were manipulated by the School Committee into supporting a predetermined outcome in the Devotion School renaming process.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the renaming process was secretive and opaque, and that selection criteria were not followed due to a predisposition toward a particular name.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, and we therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged school department employees acted improperly while supervising the Student Nominations Committee.
allegations.key_passage: However, since the Open Meeting Law only applies to public bodies, not municipal employees, we decline to review these allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Student Nominations Committee failed to follow Open Meeting Law requirements.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Student Nominations Committee lacked authority to make binding recommendations or even to deliberate on its own, we find that it was not empowered to act collectively and is not a public body under the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
